Assume water at 20°C with a density of 1000 kg/m³ and a dynamic viscosity of 0.001 Pa·s.
Assume the pipe is straight and horizontal with no fittings or minor losses.
Calculate the cross-sectional area using the internal diameter of 50 mm.
Calculate the flow velocity as the volumetric flow rate divided by the cross-sectional area.
Calculate the Reynolds number to confirm turbulent flow.
Calculate the relative roughness as the surface roughness divided by the pipe diameter.
Calculate the Darcy friction factor using the Colebrook equation with a roughness of 0.15 mm.
Calculate the pressure drop using the Darcy-Weisbach equation.
The predicted pressure drop over the 100 m length is approximately 30 kPa.
